pr_body:
The markdown output width seems too wide.  For example for `gh pr view`, it would be desirable to limit to 80 columns.  This makes it more readable for some users that have a preference for narrower paragraphs.

In #6016 the maxwidth was changed from 80 to 120.  The current code appears to use `TerminalWidth()` (pkg/iostreams/iostreams.go) which populates from termios (ie `TIOCGWINSZ`), but won't exceed the hardcoded value of 120 as set in `WithWrap()` (pkg/markdown/markdown.go).

This patch adds an environment variable override, `$GH_MDWIDTH`, similar to how `$MANWIDTH` is used to set the display width of man pages.  The default remains at 120.

Without the patch, my workaround is like so:
```
script -qc "sh -c 'stty columns 80; gh pr view 1234'" /dev/null
```

It seems like the tool should have its own setting rather than hardcode it.  The other option would be to use a `gh config` setting, but the env var is really simple and obvious, and has precedent with other tools (like `man`).

Please apply, thanks.

Fixes #9627
pr_comments: Hey @smemsh, I think this generally makes sense to me but can you create an issue to track this and as a place for us to iron out the details? We ask for this in our [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/trunk/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md#contributing) just so that we have an artifact separate from the code change about higher level design input. Cheers!
@williammartin Apologies, figured it was too trivial to write a separate issue, didn't realize that was part of the workflow.  Noted and done in #9627.
added help text for the new env var to `pkg/cmd/root/help_topic.go`

issue_context.title: max width of markdown is hardcoded, should be configurable
issue_context.body:
### Description

The maximum width of Markdown renders on the terminal (example: `gh pr view` output) is currently the lower of the actual terminal width or 120.  It should have a configurable maximum rather than being hardcoded, for those of us that prefer narrower paragraphs.

### Proposed solution

Suggest to check an environment variable for override of the 120 hardcode.  If not present, the existing default 120 will be used.  Alternative idea would be a `gh config` variable.

Environment variable is my preference as it's easy to put in one's shell profile, standard method for many terminal apps, and configures any system without having to run a config command on each one (the usual deposit of shell profile would happen anyways).  An example of analogous variable is `$MANWIDTH`.

Suggested variable name is `$GH_MDWIDTH`.  The `GH_` prefix appears to be used by a few other environment variables already.

### Additional context

A patch is proposed already at #9626.  The previous hardcode of 80 was raised to 120 in #6016.
comments:
One of my favorite debatable topics, @smemsh! 😆 In all seriousness, line length or text width is a genuine concern especially as [lines longer than 80 characters have been considered as inaccessible by W3C](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/page-structure/styling/).

> Environment variable is my preference as it's easy to put in one's shell profile, standard method for many terminal apps, and configures any system without having to run a config command on each one (the usual deposit of shell profile would happen anyways). An example of analogous variable is $MANWIDTH.
> 
> Suggested variable name is $GH_MDWIDTH. The GH_ prefix appears to be used by a few other environment variables already.

I agree if we adopted this we'd want to give users the ability to set it via env var or `gh config`, also that we prefer prefixing our env vars to avoid conflicting with others.

### Questions

1. **How many [commands rendering markdown](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Acli%2Fcli+%22markdown.Render%22&type=code) are in scope?**

   All of the following commands render Markdown in different ways:

   - `gh gist view`
   - `gh issue view`
   - `gh issue view --comments`
   - `gh pr create`
   - `gh pr review`
   - `gh pr view`
   - `gh pr view --comments`
   - `gh project view`
   - `gh reference`
   - `gh release view`
   - `gh repo view`
   - `gh workflow view`

1. **Is this contained to `gh` or to any extension using [`cli/go-gh`](https://github.com/cli/go-gh/blob/267e1ca3975c6fa25e966793442703b4c4c7ece5/pkg/markdown/markdown.go#L52-L64)?**

1. **Does this need to account for offset rendering?**

   Some of the commands above specify without indentation, however there are places where content is wrapped but it is indented.

   For example, `gh issue view https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/9627 --comments` will render the issue body as well as the comments, which are wrapped by text width and indented.

The only other thought I want to toss out is following more of the [`$LINES` and `$COLUMNS` conventions used by Bash](https://github.com/bminor/bash/blob/142bbdd89e4d5bb62aea4469d1d2c24cf470afd8/variables.c#L1040-L1059),  `lines` and `cols` used by `termcap`.

My concern with width nomenclature is that it doesn't convey units where most terminals / shells / CLIs deal in terms of columns and lines.

> One of my favorite debatable topics

It becomes less controversial when it's only opt-in, user-settable, and we don't change the existing default.

>  lines longer than 80 characters have been considered as inaccessible by W3C

(If only that applied to source code lines! :wink:)

> How many commands rendering markdown are in scope? All of the following commands render Markdown in different ways

It would be all callers of `markdown.Render()` that pass `markdown.WithWrap()`, which is where my proposed patch applies.  Your list is correct, but they don't render differently that I can tell, they all pass `markdown.WithWrap()` and all pass terminal width, except `workflow/view/view.go` is passing `0` as the wrap width, which means "don't wrap at all," because that use case probably knows better.  Likewise `root/help_reference.go` passes terminal width if a tty, else wrap `0`.  And I don't think `--comments` variants render any differently, they just show all rather than only the last comment.

(Aside: none of the commands wrap anyways if output isn't a terminal -- for example, is a pager -- which is really a bug, it should only consider whether *stdin* is a tty, not stdout.  But that would be a separate issue.)

Terminals are already of variable width, and some people do still use 80 column terminals (perhaps tiling them).  Those people will get the 80 column behavior without any changes, so they already encounter whatever issues that width would have.  This proposal is only for people that want to set an upper limit, despite their terminal width.

> Does this need to account for offset rendering? Some of the commands above specify without indentation, however there are places where content is wrapped but it is indented.

It seems to already work correctly, for example if I set width 40 then all the right margins align the same, including comments and accounting for indent.  There's a couple stray miswraps like this (shown here with 60):
```
  │ Environment variable is my preference as it's easy to
  │ put in one's shell profile, standard method for many
  │ terminal apps, and configures any system without
  having
  │ to run a config command on each one (the usual deposit
  │ of shell profile would happen anyways). An example of
  │ analogous variable is $MANWIDTH.Suggested variable
  name
  │ is $GH_MDWIDTH. The GH_ prefix appears to be used by a
  │ few other environment variables already.
```
but those already exist, I see one with it set to 80, and also at 120 (ie without changing anything), and none at 40, so there is probably a math error in there somewhere, or like you said somewhere not accounting for indentation.  But it's already there, and I would consider it a separate issue.  I don't think the patch as written introduces any new bugs, and is opt-in.  It only allows to override a hardcode which is somewhat arbitrary.

> Is this contained to gh or to any extension using cli/go-gh?

The former.  I'm only proposing to change this particular user of `ghMarkdown.WithWrap()`, not within go-gh.

> [use some naming based on the idea of columns rather than width]

Yeah, I did show the precedent of `$MANWIDTH`, but I'm indifferent to the naming and we can change it to anything that works.  Personally I think "width" is more descriptive of what's going on.  It's a terminal, so we already know that the addressing dimensions are lines and columns of character cells.  That said, any naming scheme works for me!

review_comments:
If I understand this correctly, if the `GH_MDWIDTH` variable isn't set this will return an error and set the default width to 120. Should we be a bit more explicit, here, for failures? What if the user tried to set the variable and set it incorrectly (i.e. not a number)? Should we let them know?

I'm on the fence about it, so looking for your thoughts.

The observed behavior is:

- not set: default value
- random text: default value
- negative number: gets treated like 0
- positive number: sets the default width

To me that's totally fine and like I would expect.  I don't see any need to inform the user about anything, the mismatch in their expectation vs reality will tell them they used the variable incorrectly.  But the correct usage is fairly obvious and if the user is using the variable at all they probably know to use an integer (it's also in the help text).

The code should handle bogus inputs for safety reasons, of course, but seems to already have the correct behavior in this regard.

Let me know if you concur.  Thanks for reviewing.
